criteria.description: Anchors the critique to the design's goal (start a session quickly) and user, judging points against that rather than personal taste.
Each point is specific and actionable (the concrete change to make), not vague advice like 'improve the layout'.
Separates must-fix from should-fix/polish (or otherwise prioritizes), rather than a flat equal list — e.g. flags the buried 'Start' as a top issue.
Covers multiple relevant dimensions (goal/flow, hierarchy, usability, states, content, accessibility) rather than one narrow angle.
Names strengths to keep and/or asks about unclear intent rather than only listing problems or assuming.
